premise_check.method: Grouped the three unemployment source IDs by adjustment and compared 2021-Q3 with maxima within calendar 2021 and the full supported window.
premise_check.conclusion: 2021-Q3 is not the maximum for any of the six overall, resident or citizen series, whether seasonally adjusted or unadjusted, in either comparison window. This does not identify which series the unavailable live turn selected.

evidence.paraphrase: MOM identifies business restructuring as the leading layoff reason. The quarter-on-quarter fall was spread across industries, with manufacturing contributing most.

MOM describes recovering demand as travel and dining rules eased. It also warns that uneven sector recovery can make job matching harder for older or less-qualified displaced workers, explaining persistently high long-duration resident unemployment. This does not isolate a causal effect on the headline rate.

MOM attributes the quarterly resident unemployment increase to more short-duration unemployment, rather than rising long-duration unemployment. This is a descriptive decomposition, not identification of a policy cause.

MOM reports industry downturn as the leading reason, accounting for 59% in 2020. Pandemic-exposed aviation, recreation and administrative services were particularly affected; firms reduced costs in weak conditions. Respondents could select multiple reasons.

MOM places improving unemployment alongside a broad recovery, stronger resident employment and increased hiring as economic growth accelerated. Border controls constrained foreign labour supply. This provides reported context, not a quantified causal decomposition.
MOM identifies business restructuring as the leading 2021 layoff reason, linked to preparing for growth, unlike the downturn-related pattern in 2020.

evidence.locator: section: Labour Market Advance Release 2022, item 7
evidence.paraphrase: The advance release attributes improving unemployment to economic recovery and labour-market tightness. Its published annual unemployment averages are separate source measures, not averages calculated from quarterly end-period rates.
MOM again identifies restructuring as the leading layoff reason. Downturn explanations became less prevalent; supply disruption and rising costs did not produce a proportionate increase in layoffs.

evidence.locator: section: Labour Market Report Third Quarter 2022, item 9
evidence.paraphrase: MOM links most of the quarterly increase to technology firms and interprets continued high vacancies as suggesting restructuring. Preserve that tentative interpretation, rather than presenting it as proven causation.
MOM locates most layoffs in information and communications, wholesale and electronics manufacturing, describes external economic headwinds, and identifies restructuring as the leading reason.

schema_findings: Structured and native planner schemas previously allowed any integer for k, whereas the runtime only accepts 1 through 10. All 26 unique k errors were excessive integers; observed range 83 to 86030615.
One unique missing-query event also carried statistics-tool fields despite naming search_reports. No evidence supports aliases, integer coercion or clamping.

q2_2026_retrenchment_drivers_follow_up.question_shape: Why did layoffs increase in 2Q 2026: AI displacement or COVID?
q2_2026_retrenchment_drivers_follow_up.method: Offline only. Loaded local passages, built merge200 chunks and BM25Index with default BM25Config; queried four period+topic wordings (reasons/restructuring/downturn/AI, 2026-Q2 and 2Q 2026). No embeddings, reranking, keys, network or model calls. No tests executed. Wording below is paraphrased; no publisher quotation exceeds six words.

claimed_increase_check.finding: Retrenchments rose between 1Q 2026 and 2Q 2026 (3,830 to 4,500 in the advance release, 3,830 to 4,620 in the final report and release). The final report puts the incidence at 1.6 rising to 2.0 per 1,000 staff. The two headline counts differ; the final one supersedes the advance.
claimed_increase_check.caveat: The question does not say which comparison period it means; the preceding quarter is the publisher's own comparison. Rounding is to the nearest 10 in the report.

stated_drivers.paraphrase: MOM ties the rise mainly to a few export-facing sectors (three are named) and says restructuring was again the top reason employers gave. Firms may give more than one reason.
The report summary repeats that the increase was in outward-oriented sectors and that restructuring remained the main reason.

The final press release attributes the increase to business reorganisation and restructuring in those outward-oriented sectors, and separately reports that the six-month re-entry rate for retrenched residents fell while the twelve-month rate was broadly stable.

stated_drivers.locator: section: Retrenchments rose but remained concentrated in outward-oriented sectors, item 1
stated_drivers.paraphrase: The advance release also describes the rise as concentrated in some outward-oriented sectors and driven mainly by restructuring, and says the level stayed below typical downturn levels. It is superseded by the final figures.

ai_and_covid_search.covid_context: One MOM Q2 2026 advance passage (mom-2026-q2-advance:s09:i006:b3e95f5a) lists past retrenchment ranges for two earlier downturns, including the pandemic. It is a level comparison, not a stated driver of the Q2 2026 increase.
ai_and_covid_search.ai_context: The nearest AI passages are the separate MTI Economic Survey feature on AI and employment (mti-2026-q2-feature-ai-employment, e.g. p.5, p.14, p.15). They are not period-specific MOM retrenchment explanations: the study covers firm AI use up to 2024 and its own caveat says it reflects early AI effects. They rank for lexical overlap on AI, so a generic query can retrieve them.
ai_and_covid_search.conclusion: No local MOM Q2 2026 retrenchment passage attributes the increase to AI displacement or to COVID. An answer can attribute restructuring in outward-oriented sectors to MOM and state that AI and COVID are not named as drivers there; it must not conclude that AI is not a cause.

retrieval_observation.note: Queries containing only period, retrenchment and reasons/restructuring ranked the mom-2026-q2-final p.17 chunk, p.7 summary, and final-release main findings above older reports for other years. Adding 'AI' to the query pulled in the MTI AI feature and an older MOM job vacancy release, which is the loosely related AI evidence a causal question can surface.
retrieval_observation.chunk_note: The p.17 chunk that holds the driver sentence also holds many unrelated footnote/table-fragment passages, so a total passage budget must preserve returned chunk rank and per-source diversity rather than only the first passages of each chunk.

q2_2026_retrenchment_drivers_follow_up.limits: BM25 lexical rank only, local snapshot of corpus v4 on 2026-11-03. This does not test the live reranker or any model. The final report URL is the canonical_url in data/manifests/manifest.json; the final-release and advance-release passages carry no URL in the passage records and are identified by source_id.

recommended_planner_instruction: For a why, reasons or drivers question, search_reports can retrieve publisher explanations. Use a short query containing the period, topic and words such as reasons or restructuring. k is the number of ranked chunks, from 1 to 10; use 8, never append a year or other digits. If an argument error occurs, correct the named argument within the existing call budget; do not repeat the same invalid call. For search_reports supply only query and k, not statistics filters.
recommended_answer_instruction: Distinguish an unsupported causal inference from an explanation explicitly attributed to the publisher. When passages state reasons or drivers, summarise those reasons with citations, preserving qualifiers such as suggests and separating source interpretation from established causal effects. Do not blanket-abstain on why questions when relevant publisher explanations exist. If only contextual associations are supported, provide those as context and state that the evidence does not establish a causal effect. Never treat a missing or failed tool call as proof that a report contains no explanation.
